request.system:
You answer a question about machines at work using ONLY the documents in the current folder: EU and
Italian law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, a company's documents and a plant's records, one text file per
document. README.md lists them. Use your tools (Glob, Grep, Read) to find and read what you need; search in
English and in Italian, since the documents are in both languages.

Rules:
- Use only what the files say. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- If the files do not answer the question, the kind is "unknown" and the value is null.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with the dates in the files.
- If the question asks "which" or "what" and several things answer it, list every one of them.
- If the question asks who does something and within what time, the kind is "text" and the value names both.
- When you have the answer, or are sure the files do not hold it, reply with JSON only, nothing before or after:
  {"kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "sources": [{"file": "<file name>", "place": "<heading of the section>", "quote": "<the sentence relied on, copied>"}]}
request.question: Which cleaning agents does the UR10e manual indicate for cleaning the robot arm and/or the Teach Pendant?

response.text: {"kind": "set", "value": ["Water", "70% Isopropyl alcohol", "10% Ethanol alcohol", "10% Naphtha"], "text": "The UR10e manual lists four cleaning agents for dust, dirt or oil on the robot arm and/or Teach Pendant: water, 70% isopropyl alcohol, 10% ethanol alcohol, and 10% naphtha (for grease), in section 18 Maintenance and Repair, Cleaning Methods (p. 215). Separately, section 18.3 (p. 218) says for the Teach Pendant touch screen to use a mild industrial cleaning agent without thinning agents or abrasives, and that Universal Robots does not promote a specific cleaning agent.", "sources": [{"file": "ur10e-manual.md", "place": "18. Maintenance and Repair - Cleaning Methods (p. 215)", "quote": "To address the dust, dirt, or oil on the robot arm and/or Teach Pendant, simply use a cloth alongside one of the cleaning agents provided below. ... Cleaning agents: • Water • 70% Isopropyl alcohol • 10% Ethanol alcohol • 10% Naphtha (Use to remove grease.)"}, {"file": "ur10e-manual.md", "place": "18. Maintenance and Repair - 18.3 Cleaning TP and CB (p. 218)", "quote": "Use a mild, industrial cleaning agent without thinning agents or any aggressive additives. Do not use an abrasive material to wipe down the screen. Universal Robots does not promote a specific cleaning agent."}]}
